title: 7 Best Inverter Generators (2026): Watts, Noise and Run Time
description: The Honda EU2200i is the best inverter generator for most, rated 48 to 57 dBA at about 47 lb; the Westinghouse iGen4500 gives 3,700 running watts. 7 picks.
dek: The Honda EU2200i is the best inverter generator for most, rated 48 to 57 dBA at about 47 lb; the Westinghouse iGen4500 gives 3,700 running watts.
intro: The best inverter generator for most people in 2026 is the **[Honda EU2200i](/gear/honda-eu2200i/)**. The inverter generator to buy if you want it to start every time for years and run quietly next to a neighbor's window.
Seven quiet, fuel-efficient generators compared on what the makers actually publish: running watts, decibels, run time, weight and safety features.
An inverter generator is the one you can live next to. The question is how many watts you need, and how honest the decibel number on the box is.
quickAnswer: The Honda EU2200i Super Quiet Inverter Generator is our #1 pick (best overall). The inverter generator to buy if you want it to start every time for years and run quietly next to a neighbor's window.

picks.label: Best Overall
writeup: The EU2200i is the inverter generator every other brand gets compared to, and it earns the top spot for unglamorous reasons: it starts, it keeps starting, and Honda dealers who can service it are everywhere. Honda rates it at 1,800 running and 2,200 starting watts from its GXR120 engine, enough for a refrigerator plus lights, internet, phone charging and a TV, or a gas furnace blower with a few lights. Noise is rated at 48 dBA at quarter load and 57 dBA at rated load, among the quietest figures in the class. Honda lists run time at about 3.2 hours at full rated load and 8.1 hours at quarter load on a 0.95-gallon tank, so plan fuel around that. At 47.4 lb dry, one adult can carry it to the truck or up basement steps. CO-MINDER monitors carbon monoxide and shuts the engine down if it builds up, a backup to proper placement. Two units can be paralleled for more output. The catch is price: you pay a clear premium over Champion and WEN units with similar numbers.

Quietest rating here at quarter load, 48 dBA
About 47 lb, a true one-person carry

Parallels with a second unit for more output

picks.label: Best for Home Backup
writeup: The iGen4500 fills the gap most home-backup buyers fall into: too much load for a suitcase inverter, but no wish to listen to an open-frame engine all night. Westinghouse rates it at 3,700 running and 4,500 peak watts, which covers a refrigerator, a freezer, a gas furnace blower, a sump pump, lights and electronics together if you stagger motor starts. Because it is an inverter, the engine throttles down at light load, which is why Westinghouse lists up to 18 hours at quarter load and 15 hours at half load on its 3.4-gallon tank, the longest run time on this list. Noise is rated as low as 52 dBA. Electric start with a remote key fob is a real comfort in a February storm, and the LED data center shows load, fuel level and remaining run time. The limits are its weight, close to 100 lb on wheels and a telescoping handle, and its 120V-only panel, which rules out a 240V well pump. If you want carbon monoxide shutoff, buy the iGen4500c variant, which adds CO sensing.
pros: Most running watts among the enclosed inverters here
Up to 18 hours at quarter load on a 3.4-gallon tank
Remote key-fob start
Rated as low as 52 dBA
Can start a window air conditioner alongside essentials
cons: Close to 100 lb, so it rolls rather than carries
CO sensing comes on the iGen4500c version, not the base model

picks.label: Best Value
writeup: Champion's ultralight 2500-watt inverter delivers most of what the Honda does for much less money. Champion rates it at 1,850 running and 2,500 starting watts, so its surge headroom is slightly better than the EU2200i for refrigerator and small pump starts. Retail listings put it at roughly 39 to 40 lb, the lightest on this list and the easiest to carry up stairs or into a truck bed, and it runs on a 79cc engine. The CO Shield system shuts the engine off if carbon monoxide accumulates around it, and it is parallel ready with another Champion inverter for more output. What you give up is the long track record of Honda and Yamaha engines and the depth of their dealer networks, though Champion's own support has a good reputation. The small tank also means overnight runs work best at light loads, like a refrigerator and a modem. Owners commonly describe it as easy to start and pleasantly quiet, with the usual small-engine caveat that monthly runs and stabilized fuel keep it that way. For a first inverter on a budget, it is the default answer.

picks.label: Most Watts per Dollar
writeup: The GP3500iO splits the difference between suitcase inverters and full-size portables. Generac rates it at 3,000 running and 3,500 starting watts, and its PowerRUSH feature is designed to help start motor loads such as a sump pump or a window air conditioner that a 2,200-watt unit might struggle with. That makes it a reasonable choice for a refrigerator, a freezer, a sump pump and lights together if you stagger the start-ups. Generac lists 8 hours at half load and 11 hours at quarter load on a 2.37-gallon tank, and Economy mode throttles the engine down to save fuel and cut noise at light loads. Output is inverter-clean, so laptops, TVs and furnace control boards are safe on it. The open frame keeps the cost and the 74.3 lb weight down compared with an enclosed design, but it lets more engine noise out, so it is not the one to run beside a neighbor's bedroom. It is parallel capable with Generac's kit, sold separately. Generac does not publish a decibel figure for this model in its spec sheet, so if quiet is your top priority, look at an enclosed inverter instead.

PowerRUSH helps start motor loads like sump pumps

picks.label: Best Budget Electric Start
writeup: WEN has built a large following by selling inverter generators with mid-size output at prices well below the big names, and the 56380i is its sweet spot. WEN rates it at 3,400 running and 3,800 surge watts from a 212cc OHV engine, which covers a refrigerator, a freezer, lights, internet and a furnace blower with some staggering. WEN lists noise at 57 dBA at quarter load and run time of up to 8.5 hours at half load. Electric start with a recoil backup is unusual at this price, and the fuel shutoff valve lets you run the carburetor dry before storage, which is the single best habit for a generator that sits most of the year. It is compatible with WEN's 56421 parallel kit. The trade-offs are real. WEN's published specs do not list a carbon monoxide shutoff, so placement and indoor CO alarms carry all the safety weight. At 99.2 lb it is as heavy as the Westinghouse iGen4500 with less output, and WEN's service network is thinner than Honda's or Generac's. For a buyer who wants push-button convenience and 3,000-plus watts on a budget, it is a sensible pick.

picks.label: Best Premium Step-Up
writeup: The EU3200i is Honda's answer to buyers who love the EU2200i but keep bumping into its 1,800-watt ceiling. Retail spec listings rate it at 3,200 maximum and 2,600 running watts from a Honda GX130 engine, roughly 44 percent more continuous output than the EU2200i in a package that still weighs only about 59 lb dry. That extra margin is what lets a refrigerator, a chest freezer and a gas furnace blower run together without tripping the overload light every time two compressors start at once. Noise is listed at 54 dBA at quarter load and 58 dBA at rated load, very close to the smaller Honda. Run time is about 3.3 hours at rated load and 8.6 hours at quarter load on a 1.2-gallon tank. CO-MINDER shuts the generator down if carbon monoxide builds to unsafe levels around it. Two units can be paralleled for up to 6,400 watts with Honda's kit. The downsides are price and the recoil-only start. If you can live with 1,800 watts, the EU2200i is better value; if you cannot, this is the quiet, carryable step up.

sections.h: Best Inverter Generator at a Glance

blocks.p: An inverter generator is the right portable for anyone who has to live next to it. It is quieter than a conventional open-frame generator, it burns less fuel at light load, and its output is clean enough for laptops, TVs, furnace control boards and medical devices. The trade-off is fewer watts per dollar, and most models are 120V only.

Our pick for most people is the **Honda EU2200i**: rated at 48 to 57 dBA, about 47 lb, with CO-MINDER shutoff and a reliability record nobody else matches. If you need more output for home backup, the **Westinghouse iGen4500** gives 3,700 running watts and up to 18 hours on a tank at quarter load. On a budget, the **Champion 2500-Watt Ultralight** is the value pick and the lightest on this list, and the **WEN 56380i** gets you 3,400 running watts with electric start for much less than the big names.

This guide sits inside our broader [home generator guide for power outages](/best-home-generator-for-power-outages/), which compares inverters with standby units, big open-frame portables and battery stations. If you are still deciding what kind of backup you need, read that first. If you already know you want a quiet portable, the picks are below.
THE RULE
Buy for running watts, compare on the same noise distance.
Running watts decide what you can power. Decibel ratings only compare fairly when the load and the measuring distance match, and makers do not always say which they used.
Every figure in the table comes from the manufacturer's spec sheet or listing. Where a maker does not publish a number, we say so rather than guess.

The table splits naturally into two groups. The 2,000-watt class, the Honda EU2200i, Champion 2500 and Yamaha EF2200iS, is about portability: under 60 lb, quiet, and enough for a refrigerator plus small loads. The 3,000-watt-plus class, the iGen4500, GP3500iO, WEN 56380i and EU3200i, is about home backup: enough to run a refrigerator, a freezer and a furnace blower together, at the cost of weight in most cases.
The Honda EU3200i is the outlier, with 2,600 running watts at about 59 lb. It is the only model here that adds meaningful output without becoming a wheeled unit, which is why it costs what it does.

sections.h: What Makes an Inverter Generator Different

blocks.p: A conventional portable generator spins its engine at a fixed speed, usually 3,600 rpm, because the alternator has to turn at exactly that speed to make 60 Hz power. The engine runs flat out whether you are powering a single lamp or a well pump. That is why open-frame generators are loud and thirsty at light load.

An inverter generator makes raw AC at whatever speed the engine is turning, converts it to DC, then uses electronics to rebuild a clean 60 Hz sine wave. Because the frequency no longer depends on engine speed, the engine can slow down when demand drops. Honda calls this Eco Throttle, Yamaha calls it economy control, and Generac calls it Economy mode, but the idea is the same. At light load, the engine idles down, fuel use falls, and noise drops sharply.

The electronics also produce cleaner power. Total harmonic distortion, a measure of how far the waveform strays from a perfect sine wave, is typically low on inverters; Westinghouse lists under 3 percent for its dual fuel iGen4500DF, for example. That matters for sensitive electronics, variable-speed furnace blowers and some medical equipment, which can misbehave or be damaged on rough power.

Most inverters also come in enclosed, sound-dampened cases with mufflers designed for quiet. The Generac GP3500iO is an exception, an open-frame inverter that keeps the clean power and throttle-down economy but skips the enclosure to save cost and weight.

What inverters give up is raw output per dollar. A 9,000-watt open-frame generator can cost less than a 3,700-watt inverter. If you need 240V for a well pump or want to feed most of a house through a 50-amp inlet, a conventional or dual fuel portable is the better tool; our [best dual fuel generator guide](/best-dual-fuel-generator/) covers those.

sections.h: Buying Guide: Watts, Run Time, Weight and Safety

blocks.p: List what you want to power at the same time and add up the running watts, then add the largest single starting surge. A modern refrigerator, a modem, a few LED lights and phone chargers usually fit inside 1,800 running watts. Add a chest freezer and a gas furnace blower and you need closer to 3,000. Add a sump pump or a window air conditioner and the 3,500 to 4,500-watt class makes more sense. Do not plan to run an inverter at 100 percent for hours; leave roughly 20 percent headroom.

Manufacturers usually quote run time at quarter load, which flatters every inverter. Look at the half-load or rated-load figure too. The EU2200i runs about 8.1 hours at quarter load but about 3.2 hours at full rated load. If you want to run a refrigerator overnight without refueling, a larger tank like the iGen4500's 3.4 gallons or the EF2200iS's 1.24 gallons with a fuel gauge makes life easier.

The 2,000-watt class weighs about 40 to 55 lb and can be carried by one adult. Above 3,000 watts, most inverters weigh 75 to 100 lb and roll on wheels. Think about where it lives between outages and where it will run. Steps, gravel and wet grass matter.

Parallel capability lets you link two matched units for more output later. Electric start helps in cold weather and for anyone who struggles with a pull cord. All three are worth weighing alongside the wattage.

sections.h: How Quiet Is Quiet? Reading dBA Ratings

blocks.p: Quiet is the main reason people buy inverters, and it is also the spec most open to marketing. A decibel rating means little without two other facts: the load at the time and the distance from the generator. Honda and Yamaha publish a range from quarter load to rated load, which is the honest way to do it. Others publish a single best-case figure, usually at light load, sometimes described as as low as.

Distance changes the number a lot. Sound level falls by roughly 6 dB each time you double the distance from a small source in open air. Yamaha states that its 57 to 65 dBA figures are measured at 7 meters, about 23 feet. A rating taken closer would read higher for the same machine. When a listing does not state the distance, treat comparisons as rough.

Decibels are also logarithmic. A 10 dB increase sounds roughly twice as loud to most people. So the gap between an inverter at 52 to 57 dBA and an open-frame generator rated around 74 dBA is not a small one; the open frame sounds several times louder. That is the difference between a hum your neighbor tolerates and one they complain about.

In practice, the generator's load matters more than its badge. Any inverter gets louder as it works harder, because the engine speeds up. Running a refrigerator and lights keeps it near its quarter-load rating; starting a window air conditioner pushes it toward the rated-load figure. If your street is tight, size up a little so the generator spends more of its time throttled down.

Placement helps more than most accessories. Point the exhaust and the open side away from the houses, keep the generator off hard surfaces that reflect sound, and remember that the 20-foot carbon monoxide distance discussed below also puts more air between you and the noise.

sections.h: Parallel Kits: Two Small Inverters vs One Big One

blocks.p: Most inverters on this list can be paralleled: two matched units connected with a parallel cable or kit act like one generator with roughly double the output. Two Honda EU2200i units give about 3,600 running watts, and Honda lists two EU3200i units at up to 6,400 watts. Yamaha's Twin Tech cable links two EF2200iS units for 30 amps of rated power.

The appeal is flexibility. Each unit stays light enough to carry on its own, you can take one camping and leave one home, and if one fails during an outage you still have the other. You can also start with one and add a second when budget allows.

The downsides are cost and convenience. Two premium 2,200-watt units usually cost more than a single 4,500-watt inverter, and you now have two engines to maintain, two tanks to fill and a cable to manage. Paralleling also does not give you 240V; the output is still 120V. For most homeowners who want around 3,500 to 4,000 watts and never plan to carry the generator far, a single iGen4500-class unit is simpler. For RV owners, campers and anyone who values portability, two small inverters are a strong setup.
Always pair matching models from the same brand, use the manufacturer's parallel kit, and follow its instructions for grounding and startup. Mixing brands or models is not supported.

sections.h: Using an Inverter Generator for Home Backup

blocks.p: An inverter generator can absolutely carry a house through an outage, as long as the plan matches its output. The typical approach is extension cords from the generator to the refrigerator, freezer, a lamp or two, the modem and phone chargers. With 3,000 watts or more you can add a sump pump, a furnace blower or a window air conditioner.

Feeding the house panel is harder. Most inverters, including every model on this list, have 120V outlets only, and many have no 30-amp locking outlet at all. That rules out a 240V well pump and limits what a transfer switch can do. Where a model has a 120V 30-amp outlet, an electrician may be able to wire a transfer switch or inlet configured for 120V service, but you need to confirm compatibility with your switch. Our [transfer switch guide](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) explains the options, including a single-circuit furnace switch that works well with a small inverter.
Never backfeed the panel through a dryer or range outlet with a double-male cord. It can energize the utility lines and kill a lineworker, and it can destroy the generator when grid power returns.

If you need more than about 4,000 watts, 240V, or the ability to run on stored propane, a dual fuel open-frame generator is usually a better fit; see our [dual fuel generator picks](/best-dual-fuel-generator/), or our [dual fuel inverter generator](/best-dual-fuel-inverter-generator/) guide if you want inverter-quiet power that can also run on propane. If your needs are small and you want something even lighter, our [small generator for home guide](/best-small-generator-for-home/) narrows the field to compact units. And for overnight loads like a CPAP, pairing a quiet inverter with a [portable power station](/best-portable-power-station/) lets the generator run in the day and the battery carry the night silently, indoors.

For fuel, every pick here runs on gasoline. Use fresh, stabilized fuel, run the generator monthly, and use the fuel shutoff or run the carburetor dry before storage where the model allows it. Our [gas generator guide](/best-gas-generator/) covers safe gasoline storage in more detail, and the [home outage guide](/best-home-generator-for-power-outages/) has a full sizing worksheet.

sections.h: Carbon Monoxide Safety: Quiet Does Not Mean Safe

blocks.p: Inverter generators are quiet and smell less than open frames, which makes it tempting to run them closer to the house. Do not. A small inverter still produces carbon monoxide, an odorless gas that can kill within minutes in an enclosed space. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission estimates that, on average, nearly 80 people die each year from carbon monoxide poisoning caused by portable generators.

CPSC's guidance is to run portable generators outdoors only, at least 20 feet from the house, with the exhaust pointed away from the home and any other building people could enter, and away from doors, windows and vents. Never run one in a house, garage, basement, crawlspace or shed, even with the doors and windows open; CPSC says open windows do not provide enough ventilation. Some manuals list shorter distances, but the 20-foot guidance is the one to follow.

CO shutoff systems like Honda's CO-MINDER and Champion's CO Shield add a valuable layer: they shut the engine down if carbon monoxide builds up around the generator. They do not monitor the air inside your house. Put battery or battery-backup CO alarms on every level of the home and outside sleeping areas, and test them before storm season.

Rain is the usual reason people move a generator into a garage. A purpose-made generator tent or cover that allows open-air operation solves that properly, and a longer heavy-gauge extension cord costs far less than the alternative.

mistakes: The big number on the box is usually starting or peak watts, which the generator can deliver for only a moment. Your load list has to fit the running rating, with about 20 percent headroom. A 2,200-watt inverter is an 1,800-watt generator for anything that runs more than a few seconds.
Comparing decibel ratings that are not comparable

A rating at quarter load and 7 meters is not the same as one at rated load and closer range. Honda and Yamaha publish ranges from quarter to rated load; others give a single best-case figure. Compare like with like, and expect any inverter to get louder as the load rises.
Moving it closer because it is quiet

Quiet operation does not reduce carbon monoxide to safe levels. CPSC says to run portable generators outdoors, at least 20 feet from the house, with exhaust pointed away and away from doors, windows and vents. A garage with the door open is still indoors.
Expecting it to run a well pump or the whole panel

Every inverter on this list is 120V only. A 240V well pump, an electric range or central air needs a 240V generator, usually a big open-frame or dual fuel unit. Plan an inverter around extension cords to essentials, or a 120V-compatible transfer setup approved by an electrician.
Letting fuel sit in the carburetor

Small inverter carburetors have tiny passages that stale gasoline gums up quickly. Use fresh, stabilized fuel, run the generator under load monthly, and use the fuel shutoff to run the carburetor dry before storage on models that have one. Most no-start complaints trace back to old fuel.
bottomLine: For most buyers, the **[Honda EU2200i](/gear/honda-eu2200i/)** is still the best inverter generator: quiet, light, reliable and equipped with CO-MINDER shutoff. If you need more output for a real outage load, the **[Westinghouse iGen4500](/gear/westinghouse-igen4500/)** is the better home backup machine, and the Champion 2500 and WEN 56380i stretch a budget furthest. Whichever you choose, size it on running watts, read decibel ratings with the load and distance in mind, and run it at least 20 feet from the house with working CO alarms inside. A quiet generator is only an asset if it is also a safe one.

faqs.q: What is the best inverter generator for home use?
faqs.a: For essentials, the Honda EU2200i is our top pick for reliability, low noise and its CO-MINDER shutoff. For a fuller outage load, the Westinghouse iGen4500 offers 3,700 running watts and long run time. On a budget, the Champion 2500-Watt Ultralight or the WEN 56380i give good value for the money.

faqs.q: Is an inverter generator better than a regular generator?
faqs.a: For quiet, fuel economy at light load and clean power for electronics, yes. A regular open-frame generator gives more watts per dollar and often 240V outlets for a transfer switch or well pump. Many households are best served by an inverter for everyday outages, or a dual fuel open frame when they need big output.

faqs.q: How quiet is an inverter generator?
faqs.a: Makers rate the quietest models in the high 40s to high 50s dBA at light load. Honda lists the EU2200i at 48 to 57 dBA from quarter to rated load, Westinghouse rates the iGen4500 from 52 dBA, and WEN lists the 56380i at 57 dBA at quarter load. Open-frame generators are commonly rated around 74 dBA.

faqs.q: Can an inverter generator run a refrigerator?
faqs.a: Yes. A typical modern refrigerator runs well within the 1,800 running watts of a Honda EU2200i or Yamaha EF2200iS, and their starting surge covers the compressor start. Add a freezer, sump pump or furnace blower at the same time and a 3,000-watt-plus inverter like the GP3500iO or iGen4500 is the safer choice.

faqs.q: Can I connect an inverter generator to my house?
faqs.a: Sometimes, with limits. The models here are 120V only, so they cannot power 240V circuits like a well pump. Where a generator has a 120V 30-amp outlet, an electrician may be able to set up a compatible transfer switch or inlet. Never backfeed through a dryer outlet; it can kill utility workers.

faqs.q: How long will an inverter generator run on a tank of gas?
faqs.a: It depends heavily on load. Westinghouse lists up to 18 hours at quarter load for the iGen4500 on 3.4 gallons. Yamaha lists 10.5 hours at quarter load for the EF2200iS, and Honda lists 8.1 hours at quarter load but 3.2 hours at full rated load for the EU2200i.

faqs.q: Is it worth paralleling two inverter generators?
faqs.a: It can be. Two matched units give roughly double the output while each stays light enough to carry, and you keep a backup if one fails. The trade-offs are higher total cost, two engines to maintain and output that is still 120V only. For a single fixed home setup, one larger inverter is often simpler.
